title: Mohd. Daud v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
coram: V.K. Shukla, J. & Suneet Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy
headnote: A dispute about the correctness of a bill — here whether a bill could be raised, and recovery effected, after an alleged past permanent disconnection — is in pith and substance a billing dispute that must first be raised before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ against the demand notice was not entertained; the petitioner was left to raise the dispute before the competent authority, who will look into and redress it in accordance with law.

holding_units.topic: Billing-correctness dispute must first go to the competent authority under Clause 6.5
holding_units.question: Should a writ be entertained against a demand notice where the real grievance is that the bill itself was incorrectly raised (after an alleged permanent disconnection)?
holding_units.holding: No. The subject matter is the raising of the bill, which is a billing dispute to be raised in the first instance before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the Code. The writ is not entertained on the ground of alternative remedy; the petitioner may raise the dispute before the competent authority, who will redress it in accordance with law.

principle_tags.application: A billing-correctness grievance is relegated to the Clause 6.5 competent authority; the writ court will not entertain it at the first instance.

not_decided.point: Whether the bill was correctly raised after the alleged permanent disconnection
not_decided.note: Left open to be decided by the competent authority under Clause 6.5; the Court expressed no view on the merits.
